summary: Defines two new CDNI footprint types: a country subdivision code and a footprint union. They are meant for open caching, where a commercial CDN works with ISP caching layers, and extend footprint types from RFC 8006.

eli5.summary: Delivery networks need to say where they can serve. This adds ways to say a state or province, and to combine several areas into one.

questions: what is a country subdivision code footprint
subtitle: Two new ways to describe where a downstream CDN can serve: a state or province code, and a union that combines footprint types.

tldr.problem: CDN Interconnection footprints could name a whole country but not a state or province, and listing both IPv4 and IPv6 subnets together produced an empty footprint because multiple footprint constraints narrow each other.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds a subdivisioncode footprint type that uses ISO 3166-2 codes such as us-ny, and a footprintunion type that bundles several footprint objects so they add up instead of narrowing.
tldr.outcome: Open Caching can describe a downstream CDN's reach with finer granularity and mixed footprint types. The RFC updates RFC 8008 and registers both types with IANA.

facts.label: Subdivision code form
facts.value: country code, hyphen, up to three alphanumeric characters

today: RFC 9388 is a Proposed Standard from July 2023 and updates RFC 8008. No later RFC is listed as obsoleting or updating it.

sections.title: Why Open Caching Needs New Footprints
sections.content:
In Open Caching, a commercial Content Delivery Network (CDN) hands video delivery requests to a caching layer inside an ISP's network. In CDN Interconnection (CDNI) terms the commercial CDN is the upstream CDN (uCDN) and the ISP caching layer is the downstream CDN (dCDN).

The dCDN advertises where it can serve using footprint objects, each with a footprint type and a footprint value. RFC 8006 defines the footprint types and RFC 8008 defines the advertisement interface. This RFC registers two more types: a country subdivision code, and a footprint union that groups footprints built from several types.
sections.eli5: A big video company asks a local internet provider to help deliver videos. The provider needs better ways to say which neighbourhoods it covers.

sections.title: The subdivisioncode Footprint Type
sections.content:
RFC 8006 already has a countrycode footprint type for ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes. A country is a coarse unit, so this RFC adds the subdivisioncode data type, based on ISO 3166-2 country subdivision codes.

A value is written in lowercase and has two parts separated by a hyphen. The first part is the ISO 3166-1 country code and the second part is a string of up to three alphanumeric characters. The RFC's examples are ca-on and us-ny. Its advertisement example uses the footprint value ["us-nj", "us-ny"] to match clients in New Jersey or New York.
sections.eli5: Instead of saying only the country, you can now say the state or province too, like writing the state on a letter as well as the country.

sections.title: The footprintunion Footprint Type
sections.content:
Under the semantics in Appendix B of RFC 8008, several footprint constraints in one list are additive, which narrows the dCDN's candidacy cumulatively. That breaks an obvious case: an ipv4cidr object and an ipv6cidr object in the same list can never match any client, because an address cannot be both IPv4 and IPv6. The RFC shows this as an advertisement of a null footprint.

The footprintunion type fixes this. Its footprint value is an array of footprint objects, and the union matches what any of them matches. The RFC gives two uses: an IPv4 CIDR together with an IPv6 CIDR, and a country code together with a country subdivision code. A union can sit next to other footprints in the list, for example an asn object, which still narrows as before.

A footprintunion MUST NOT list another footprintunion as a value. A union of unions is just a union, so the rule removes implementation complexity without losing expressiveness.
sections.eli5: A union is a bag that holds several lists of places. Anything on any list in the bag counts, but you cannot put a bag inside a bag.

sections.title: Representation in ALTO Property Maps
sections.content:
RFC 9241 describes how footprint objects become entities in an Application-Layer Traffic Optimization (ALTO) property map, with the footprint type as the entity domain type and the footprint value as the domain-specific identifier. This RFC extends that to subdivisioncode.

The new SUBDIVISIONCODE domain has the entity domain type subdivisioncode in lowercase. An identifier is an alpha-2 ISO 3166-1 country code, then a separator, then up to three alphanumeric characters. There is no hierarchy or inheritance for properties of country subdivision codes.
sections.eli5: The same state-code idea also works in a second system that keeps lists about network places, using the same naming rule.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content:
The RFC adds two entries to the "CDNI Metadata Footprint Types" subregistry from RFC 8006: subdivisioncode (an ISO 3166-2 code made of an alpha-2 country code, a hyphen-minus and up to 3 characters from A-Z and 0-9) and footprintunion (a combination of other footprint objects).

It also registers subdivisioncode in the "ALTO Entity Domain Types" subregistry created by RFC 9240, with hierarchy and inheritance set to None and mapping to ALTO address type set to false.
sections.eli5: The two new kinds of place lists get official names in public registries, so everyone spells them the same way.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: This specification adds no new security machinery. It is subject to the security and confidentiality considerations in Section 8 of RFC 8006 for CDNI Metadata and in Section 7 of RFC 8008 for footprint and capabilities semantics.
sections.eli5: The new place lists follow the same safety rules as the older ones, with nothing extra added.
